definitions.meal: Breakfast, lunch, or dinner consumed in the course of business travel or business activity.
definitions.incidental: Snacks, coffees, and small purchases under $10 are not meals for cap purposes.
definitions.client_entertainment: A meal or event hosted for external clients, prospects, or business partners for relationship development.
definitions.high_cost_city: A city in Lodging Tier 1 per TEP-004 §3 (Seattle, Boston, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles, Washington DC).

faq.question: Destination resort breakfast fee bundled in room rate?
faq.answer: Mandatory resort-fee breakfast is part of room rate (TEP-004 §4.2). The breakfast itself counts against the breakfast cap; reasonable overages in resort context may be manager-approved.

faq.question: Contractor colleague at team off-site — client entertainment?
faq.answer: No. Company-paid contractors are not external clients. Apply standard per-meal caps.

faq.question: Cash tip beyond receipt?
faq.answer: Tip must appear on receipt or Missing Receipt Affidavit (TEP-007 §4.2). Reimbursement remains capped at 20% per Section 3.

faq.question: Client paid check — expense at next meeting?
faq.answer: Yes, subject to standard caps and approval. Each entertainment event is evaluated independently.

rules.source_quote: High-cost city — meal caps follow Lodging Tier 1 list per TEP-004 §3.
Snacks, coffees, and small purchases under $10 are not meals for cap purposes.
Client entertainment breakfast — elevated cap applies with documented external attendees.
Client entertainment lunch — elevated cap applies with documented external attendees.
Client entertainment dinner — up to $150 per person with external attendees documented.
Multiple meals on the same calendar day may be subject to combined-cap review.
Tips above 20% of the pre-tax meal total are considered personal and are not reimbursable.
